questions.q: What are the main functions of a constitution?
answer: A constitution is the fundamental law of a country, and it performs several vital functions.

answer.text: First, it provides a set of basic rules that allow people living together to coordinate their behaviour with one another, giving society a minimum of trust and order.

Second, it specifies who has the power to make decisions and how the government is to be constituted. Third, and equally important, it sets limits on what the government can do to its citizens, guaranteeing rights that no government may violate.

Fourth, it enables the government to fulfil the aspirations of a society and create conditions for a just society. Finally, it expresses the fundamental identity of a people, declaring the values by which they wish to live together.

answer: Thus a constitution both empowers and restrains government, while embodying the ideals of the nation.

questions.q: How was the Indian Constitution framed, and why does it command authority?

answer.text: The Indian Constitution was framed by a Constituent Assembly that first met in December 1946. Over nearly three years it debated and drafted the document, with the Drafting Committee chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar and the Assembly presided over by Dr Rajendra Prasad. It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

The Constitution commands authority for several reasons. The Assembly that made it broadly represented Indian society, giving it representative credentials. Its provisions were arrived at through careful deliberation, reason and consensus rather than the mere will of a majority. It also balances flexibility with stability, allowing amendment while protecting its core values.

answer: For these reasons the Constitution has been accepted and respected as the supreme law of the land.

questions.q: Why is a constitution the supreme law of a land, and how does it both empower and limit government?

answer.text: is the fundamental document that lays down how a country is to be governed, and it stands above ordinary law.

list: It is the source from which all other laws and institutions draw their authority
No law or government action that conflicts with it is valid

answer.text: This double role is its essence.

list: It empowers the government by defining its organs and giving them the authority to act
It limits the government by fixing the boundaries of its power and guaranteeing rights that the state cannot violate

questions.q: How did the Objectives Resolution shape the values of the Indian Constitution?

answer.text: moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly, set out the ideals that would guide the making of the Constitution.

list: It declared India an independent, sovereign republic drawing its authority from the people
It promised justice, equality and freedom to all citizens and safeguards for minorities and the disadvantaged

answer.lead: It became the soul of the document.
answer.text: Its spirit runs through the Constitution.

list: Its ideals were later expressed in the Preamble
It committed India to democracy, dignity and the unity of the nation, giving the Constitution its moral foundation
